evidence.source: Hong Kong Educational University, Lexicon of Chinese Phonology
evidence.field: historical component analysis and modern pronunciation
evidence.text: This reference calls 中 the phonetic component in 貴 and gives modern Mandarin gui4 for the host. It does not provide a reading for 中 or a historical sound comparison, so the phonetic proposal remains unsupported by a sourced reading pair.
evidence.title: 字源考釋 - 貴

evidence.text: The entry analyzes the early graph as hands holding an object and notes interpretations connecting it with 遺; it also records a later 貝-related form and quotes 說文’s analysis 貝 plus phonetic 臾. This does not corroborate 中 as a phonetic in 貴. Its early-form discussion is distinct from sound evidence for 中.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：貴

evidence.source: Kim Jun-su, Korea Journal of Chinese Linguistics (2016), article record and abstract
evidence.text: The study analyzes 貴 as 貝 plus 臾, associating 臾 with the protoform of 簣. It proposes 貴 *kluds in Zhengzhang Shangfang Old Chinese and reports modified Baxter–Sagart *kut-s. Neither reconstruction supplies a reading for 中, so this is not a historical 中–貴 sound pair.
evidence.title: 《說文解字》貴聲系字의 上古音 再構에 대한 小考

search_audit.query: 貴 中 聲符 貝 中 古文字 貴 字源; 貴 中聲 上古音 中 貴 phonetic component reconstruction; site:unicode.org/cgi-bin/GetUnihanData.pl?codepoint=4E2D
search_audit.outcome: Search located the competing 中-phonetic claim, the CUHK 貴 entry, and a study supporting the traditional 臾 analysis. Opened all three pages. No historical 中–貴 reading pair was found.

Official Unihan lookup documentation opened, but each character-specific record URL failed to open in the web tool. Exact local kMandarin rows were inspected for both characters: zhōng for 中 and guì for 貴.

gaps: No historical reconstruction or period-specific reading for 中 in the proposed 貴 analysis was found; the available historical reconstructions concern 貴 and the traditional 臾 series, not 中.

The local modern Mandarin pair 中 zhōng and 貴 guì does not establish a historical phonetic relation. No Modern Mandarin pronunciation card is warranted by this component-specific task unless the interface explicitly permits reporting a nonmatching pair as contrastive only.

Official Unicode character-specific Unihan pages were attempted at the prescribed URLs but were inaccessible through the browser tool; local rows were inspected, but no accessible official click-through record was verified.
